Thanks — attached is a short proposal (atlas_capacity_proposal_v1.pdf) and an internal banding table for how we think about discounts / SKU mix (reserve_banding_table.xlsx). High level summary below so you can pull into the procurement packet quickly.

Short answers up front:
- GPU mix: for your profile we recommend a mixed pool: majority H100-optimized nodes for low-latency chat (approx 60%), supplemented by a fleet of A100-style instances for throughput batches and longer-context jobs. This typically maps to 12 H100-equivalent concurrent inference slots + 8 A100-equivalent spots at the 1x baseline.
- Commit term: 12-month standard, optional 24-month at a ~6-8% deeper rate. We can also offer a 6-month pilot at ~70% of the 12-month price with limited SLA guarantees.
- Price sensitivity / protectors: we support a GPU-price indexation clause (quarterly adjustment capped at +/-10%) or a price-pass-through with a floor; alternatively we can structure a hybrid: fixed unit rates for the first 6 months and an index thereafter.

Key tradeoffs to flag to procurement:
- Longer term (24mo): lower unit price, but we need a simple mechanism for rebalancing SKU mix if your workload shifts to favor throughput over latency. We recommend a quarterly SKU replan with a capped reconfiguration credit.
- Shorter term (6mo pilot): gives you flexibility but costs more and we can only guarantee a smaller dedicated burst pool.
- Price contingencies: indexation preserves predictability for both parties; pass-through is simpler operationally but less predictable for Atlas budgeting.

I've cc'd Karthik & Marissa to weigh in on discount thresholds and finance approval path; Ben Carter will advise on the finance signoff we should expect.

If useful I can convert the banding table into a 1-pager for the procurement deck.

Thanks,

Folks —

Quick internal note on what I recommend for the deal structure and approval ask:

Proposal that Hannah sends to Atlas should include three priced options (all normalized to equivalent H100 capacity):
1) Pilot (6 months) — 60% of the baseline capacity, no SLA, +20% unit price premium. Good for proof of scale.
2) Standard (12 months) — 100% baseline capacity, standard SLA, baseline price. Includes quarterly SKU replan (no more than 2 adjustments/year).
3) Committed (24 months) — 100% baseline + 20% burst buffer, 8% discount off baseline and priority access during capacity constraints. Includes an annual SKU rebalancing allowance and a one-time migration credit if they change regions.

On pricing sensitivity to GPU costs:
- Finance prefers an indexation model tied to a GPU cost index we maintain internally (quarter-over-quarter). We cap index adjustments at +/-10% per year and commit to a true-up mechanism so neither side unfairly benefits.
- If Atlas insists on pass-through we can accept for an additional 2% premium and a minimum floor of -5% (i.e., we won't reduce below that floor).

Approval path:
- Pilots can be approved at AE + Sales Manager level.
- Standard 12mo deals with up to $250k ARR uplift need Sales Manager + Sales Finance (Ben).
- Any >$250k ARR or 24mo with >8% discount requires RevOps + VP Sales sign-off (Marissa).

Ben — can you confirm the guidance on the ARR thresholds and whether finance wants a separate contract rider for indexation?

-karthik
Director, Deal Strategy

Confirming finance position ahead of Hannah's final send:

2) Indexation rider: finance prefers the internal GPU index approach. We will accept the +/-10% cap per year with quarterly observations. Implementation notes: we need a simple formula in the SOW (base_unit_rate * (1 + index_delta)), and a quarterly true-up invoice to reconcile. If Atlas insists on pass-through instead, add a 2% premium and implement a 3-month notice window for index changes.

3) Discount approval: 6% discount is approvable by Sales Manager and Finance for 24mo if ARR is between $250k-$750k. Any deeper (7%+) needs RevOps + VP Sales.
